chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about the newborn whose writing has not yet been done upon him, is prayer offered for him? He said:
"No, rather prayer is offered for the man and the woman only when the writing has been done upon them."
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever catches one takbirah for the deceased or two, he completes it.

key_terms.الصَّلاَةُ: Prayer (specifically funeral prayer in this context)
key_terms.جَرَى عَلَيْهِ الْقَلَمُ: When the writing (of deeds/record) has been done upon him

ai.seo_question: Is funeral prayer offered for a newborn baby who has not yet had their 'qalam' written?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes that the ritual funeral prayer (Salat al-Janazah) is contingent upon the 'qalam' (divine record of deeds) being inscribed, which for newborns occurs at a specific developmental stage rather than immediately at birth. Al-Sheikh al-Tusi supplements this with the juristic principle of 'joining the congregation' (muqasamah), ruling that catching even one or two takbirahs validates the prayer for the latecomer, reflecting the Shia emphasis on communal participation and ease in ritual obligations.
